correctness.rationale: With fixed unit edge lengths and all leaves independently surviving with common p, protection of x adds an edge e on its root path exactly when all m_e descendants originally fail, with probability q^{m_e}. The resulting polynomial sum is exact for every q=1−p in (0,1). Cumulative dominance of clade-size incidence vectors implies all-q dominance by discrete summation by parts. Independently generated canonical unordered rooted binary tree shapes n=2..8 have counts 1,1,2,3,6,11,23; none below eight lacks a globally cumulatively dominant leaf and exactly one at n=8 does. The eight-leaf exceptional shape has path profiles (3,1),(3,2,1),(5,1),(5,4,2,1), with the longer two dominant and difference R−L=q^3(q²+q−1). Thus the unique survival switch is p=(3−sqrt(5))/2 and the claimed numbers of maximizing leaves follow. Exhaustive n<=8 shape classification is finite and complete by child-pair recursion; the polynomial argument covers the entire continuum of p.
residual_risks: The sharp cutoff assumes equal independent survival risks, unit edges, rooted binary non-plane trees, and protecting exactly one taxon; heterogeneous lengths/rates can change the result.

originality.rationale: The HED/HEDGE conservation-benefit formula is explicitly credited to prior sources, notably Steel–Mimoto–Mooers (2007). The assessed increment is the exact first topology-driven optimizer switch at eight leaves, uniqueness of its exceptional unlabelled shape and exact threshold. The 2006 Hartmann–Steel paper was not read in full; coverage of this exact sharp unit-edge classification is a residual possibility, not automatic rejection.
